title: Longest Common Block of Two Words

concept.title: Binary search on the length, keys of both words
body: Comparing two blocks of a word letter by letter costs as much as their length. A **polynomial rolling hash** turns every block into a number in O(1) after one preparation pass. Treat the letters as digits of a number in some base `B` (modulo a big prime `M`): `hash(s[l..r)) = s[l]*B^(r-l-1) + ... + s[r-1]`.

body.code:
h[i + 1] = (h[i] * B + value(s[i])) % M        # prefix hashes, one pass
block(l, r) = (h[r] - h[l] * B^(r - l)) % M       # O(1) for any block

body: Equal blocks always have equal hashes. Different blocks have different hashes with very high probability, and using **two moduli at once** makes a collision practically impossible (the two values are packed into one 62-bit number). With such keys, blocks can be put into hash sets and compared in O(1).

The longest block that occurs in **both** words has the same monotone property as before: if a block of length `L` is common, so is every shorter one. Binary search on `L`: put the keys of all blocks of length `L` of the first word into a set, and look for any block of the second word with a key in the set.
The two words are hashed with the **same** base and moduli, so equal blocks get equal keys even though they come from different words.

statement: Given two words `a` and `b`, find the length of the longest block of consecutive letters that occurs in both words. If they have no letter in common, print 0.
hints: If a block of length L is common, every shorter one is too.
For a length L, put the keys of the blocks of `a` into a set.
Check whether any block of length L of `b` has a key in the set.

explanation: Being a common block is monotone in the length. For each tested length the keys of the first word are stored in a set and the blocks of the second word are looked up.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + m) log(min(n, m))) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
M1, M2 = 1000000007, 998244353
B1, B2 = 911382323, 972663749


def build_hash(s):
    n = len(s)
    h1 = [0] * (n + 1)
    h2 = [0] * (n + 1)
    p1 = [1] * (n + 1)
    p2 = [1] * (n + 1)
    for i, ch in enumerate(s):
        v = ord(ch) - 96
        h1[i + 1] = (h1[i] * B1 + v) % M1
        h2[i + 1] = (h2[i] * B2 + v) % M2
        p1[i + 1] = p1[i] * B1 % M1
        p2[i + 1] = p2[i] * B2 % M2
    return h1, h2, p1, p2


def sub_key(hash_data, l, r):
    h1, h2, p1, p2 = hash_data
    a = (h1[r] - h1[l] * p1[r - l]) % M1
    b = (h2[r] - h2[l] * p2[r - l]) % M2
    return a * M2 + b

a = input().strip()
b = input().strip()

n, m = len(a), len(b)
da = build_hash(a)
db = build_hash(b)
lo, hi = 0, min(n, m)
while lo < hi:
    mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
    keys = {sub_key(da, i, i + mid) for i in range(n - mid + 1)}
    found = any(sub_key(db, j, j + mid) in keys for j in range(m - mid + 1))
    if found:
        lo = mid
    else:
        hi = mid - 1
print(lo)
